reason: Historical source-mode searches preserve old stable scheduling ties and Phase 5 synthesis. The new runtime mode selector needs exactly matched canonical scheduling and the new synthesis environment. Keep historical demonstrations; fit conditional costs only on this matched supplement.
boundary: Same 160 frozen development statements and same four whole-family validation groups. No final-test statements or historical held-out labels.
selection: Unchanged preregistered validation MSE on independently verified completion costs only. Both competing regressors use these matched outcomes; censored modes are retained without mathematical-negative labels.
tie_rule: All three use unchanged P3 scores then explicit tactic-string ties.
symbolic: Force symbolic selection in the same learned provider/session, canonical P3 ties; no native query.
hybrid: Force hybrid selection with already trained selected relevance, new native synthesis and canonical P3 ties.
typed: Force deterministic Phase 5 selection with new native synthesis in the same learned provider; canonical P3 ties.
sequence: Select and refit relevance using frozen family-level rules; freeze relevance coefficients; collect three fixed-mode development counterfactuals with that fitted relevance; select/refit mode regressor using the same whole-family boundary; only then freeze all execution and access final tests.
switching_limit: Targets are fixed-mode continuation costs from root development states. Final greedy per-state adaptive switching differs from those continuations; this approximation and root-state distribution shift are explicit.
ablations: Linear and applicability relevance controls share the finalized selected-model selector, isolating relevance changes; their counterfactual costs may differ from those used to fit that selector.
